title: Interpret the logarithm
text: The $$\log_{@{b}}\left(\frac{1}{@{b}}\right)$$ is that power that @{b} is raised to to get $$\frac{1}{@{b}}$$

title: Find the relationship
text: Find a power k so that $${@{b}}^k=\frac{1}{@{b}}$$

title: Full solution
text: $$\log_{@{b}}\left(\frac{1}{@{b}}\right)=k$$ is equivalent to $${@{b}}^k=\frac{1}{@{b}}$$. And the number that makes that true is $$k=-1$$. \n We can check that this makes sense since $${@{b}}^{\left(-1\right)} {@{b}}^1={@{b}}^0=1=\frac{@{b}}{@{b}}$$
